finding: A long-running Balancer with encrypted data transfer caches one DataEncryptionKey forever in NameNodeConnector; after block keys roll, DataNodes reject it in BlockTokenSecretManager.retrieveDataEncryptionKey and every replaceBlock fails (this is HDFS-11741, not HDFS-5766).
same_root_cause: No. The agent's failing execution goes through the balancer: NameNodeConnector.getDataEncryptionKey (server/balancer/NameNodeConnector.java:155-162, generates the key once when encryptionKey == null and never checks expiry) used by Balancer.dispatch (Balancer.java:344-347, logs 'Failed to move' at :361). The HDFS-5766 fix only adds `continue;` after dfsClient.clearDataEncryptionKey() in DFSInputStream.fetchBlockByteRange (DFSInputStream.java:965-971 in the buggy tree, hunk @@ -969,6 +969,7). The agent's test never performs a client positional read; the logs contain no DFSInputStream/fetchBlockByteRange frames, and the defect it hits (no key renewal in the balancer) is untouched by the fix.
realistic: Mostly realistic for the defect it does hit: MiniDFSCluster, throttled balancer bandwidth, and shortened key-update interval/token lifetime via the same test setters TestEncryptedTransfer uses (compressing the real 10h defaults). No reflection or mocks. But it is irrelevant to HDFS-5766.
fixed_version: The test still fails identically on the fixed tree (REPRODUCED, same InvalidEncryptionKeyException at BlockTokenSecretManager.java:426 from DataXceiver during balancer moves), confirming the HDFS-5766 fix does not affect this execution.
reason: The agent found a different real bug (the balancer's stale cached DataEncryptionKey, HDFS-11741) that happens to fail the same check. It never exercises DFSInputStream.fetchBlockByteRange or the missing `continue` that marks a healthy DataNode dead, and the fixed version still fails. Not a detection of HDFS-5766.
